easy.def: To have something in your hands.
examples: Hold my hand.
She holds a cup.
He held the baby.

more.def: To have something in your hands or arms, or to keep it in place.
examples: Hold the rope tightly so that you do not fall.
She held the kitten gently in her arms.
The shelf holds all of our heavy books.
I dug a hole.
There is a hole in my sock.
The mouse hid in a hole.

more.def: An opening or hollow place in something.
examples: A rabbit dug a hole under the fence.
There is a hole in my left sock.
The ball fell down a hole.
The church is a holy place.
It is a holy book.
People pray at holy places.

more.def: Connected with God or a religion, and treated with great respect.
examples: Many people travel to holy places to pray.
The temple is a holy building.
The holy book was kept in a special box.
I go home after school.
Our home is warm.
Birds make a home in the tree.

more.def: The place where a person or family lives, or where an animal lives.
examples: My grandmother's home is full of old photographs.
A hollow log is a good home for small animals.
We were glad to get home after the long trip.
Be honest. Did you eat the cookie?
An honest boy gave back the lost coin.
Please be honest with me.

more.def: Truthful; not lying, cheating, or stealing.
examples: She was honest and told the teacher that she had broken the window.
To be honest, I did not like the movie.
An honest shopkeeper gave back the extra money.

easy.def: A sweet, sticky food that bees make.
examples: I like honey on toast.
Bees make honey.
The honey is sweet.

more.def: A thick, sweet food that bees make from the nectar of flowers.
examples: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.
I stirred a spoonful of honey into my tea.
The honey dripped from the comb onto the biscuit.
It is an honor to meet you.
She had the honor of lighting the candle.
He won an honor for his bravery.

more.def: Great respect, or something that makes you feel proud.
examples: It is an honor to sing for the whole school.
She had the honor of cutting the ribbon at the new library.
He won an honor for helping the neighbors.
We honor the heroes.
The school honored her.
They honor the flag.

more.def: To show great respect for someone or something.
examples: The town held a parade to honor the firefighters.
We honor our grandparents on a special day.
The school honored her for her kindness.

easy.def: A curved piece of metal for hanging things.
examples: Hang your coat on the hook.
The pirate had a hook for a hand.
The hook is by the door.

more.def: A curved piece of metal or plastic used to hang things or catch fish.
examples: Hang your coat on the hook by the door.
The fish bit the hook.
A hook held the picture on the wall.
I hope it snows.
She hopes to win.
We hoped for sun.

more.def: To want something to happen and think that it might.
examples: I hope the rain stops before the picnic.
He is hoping to see a deer in the woods.
We hoped that our team would win the game.
I have hope.
Her hope is to swim.
Hope kept us going.

more.def: A feeling that something good may happen.
examples: The rain gave the farmers hope for a good harvest.
She held on to hope that her lost cat would come home.
Our hope is to build a new playground.

easy.def: The line far away where the sky seems to touch the land or sea.
examples: The sun went down below the horizon.
We saw a boat on the horizon.
The sun comes up over the horizon.

more.def: The line in the distance where the sky and the land or sea seem to meet.
examples: A ship appeared as a tiny dot on the horizon.
Dark clouds gathered on the horizon.
The road stretched all the way to the horizon.
The smell was horrible.
A horrible noise.
The weather is horrible.

more.def: Very bad or unpleasant.
examples: The horrible smell came from the trash.
We had horrible weather on our trip.
It was a horrible mistake.

easy.def: A large animal that people ride.
examples: We rode a horse.
The horse ate hay.
A horse can run fast.

more.def: A large, strong animal with hooves and a long mane that people ride and use to pull things.
examples: Farmers once used a horse to pull plows.
The horse galloped across the open field.
She brushed the horse's mane and gave it an apple.

easy.def: A place where doctors help sick people.
examples: The nurse works at the hospital.
My uncle was in the hospital.
We visited Grandpa at the hospital.

more.def: A building where doctors and nurses take care of people who are sick or hurt.
examples: The ambulance took her to the hospital.
My mom works as a nurse at the hospital.
Babies are born at the hospital every day.
Be careful, the soup is hot.
It is hot in the sun.
The pan is hot.

more.def: Having a very high temperature, so that it can burn you or make you sweat.
examples: The sand was so hot that we ran to the water.
Desert days are hot, but the nights can be cold.
Be careful with the hot oven when you bake.

easy.def: Having a taste that burns your mouth.
examples: This pepper is hot.
The chili was too hot for me.
Mom likes hot sauce.

more.def: Having a strong, spicy taste that burns your mouth a little.
examples: The hot salsa made my eyes water.
Some people like hot peppers on their pizza.
Jalapeños are hotter than green bell peppers.

easy.def: A building where you pay to sleep.
examples: We stayed at a hotel.
The hotel has a pool.
Our room at the hotel was big.

more.def: A building with many rooms where travelers pay to stay.
examples: We stayed in a hotel near the beach.
The hotel had a pool and a breakfast room.
A hotel clerk gave us the room key.
It takes an hour.
We waited one hour.
School is six hours long.

more.def: A length of time equal to sixty minutes.
examples: There are twenty-four hours in one day.
The drive to the beach takes about an hour.
We studied for two hours before dinner.
We have a red house.
The house has a big yard.
I walk to my friend's house.

more.def: A building where one family or a few people live.
examples: Our house has a front porch and a small garden.
The old house at the end of the street has been empty for years.
The builders worked all summer to finish the house.

easy.def: A word used to ask in what way.
examples: How do you do it?
How are you?
How old are you?

more.def: A word used to ask about the way something is done, an amount, or a feeling.
examples: How does a caterpillar turn into a butterfly?
How tall is the tree in the front yard?
Tell me how you made this paper airplane.
I like pizza. However, I am full.
It is cold. However, we played outside.
He tried. However, he failed.

more.def: Used to show a surprise or a different idea from what was just said.
examples: It was raining. However, we still went to the park.
I wanted to go. However, I was too tired.
The test was hard. However, most kids passed.
